reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism of perception is the transformation from vague totality to structured parts. Initially, a child sees a room as an undifferentiated whole. As experience accumulates, attentional mechanisms begin to parse this totality into components. This process is governed by two primary drivers: practical and aesthetic interests. These interests modulate the salience function S, determining which part of the environment receives focus. The structuration of perception is thus a dynamic interplay between vagueness V and attention A, where A acts as a selector over V to produce P. The failure mode arises when either V is too high (no structure) or A is insufficient (no parsing). This framework underpins both GSI's probabilistic belief updates and GSE's state transition logic.
